title: Reverse Linked List
summary: Reverse a singly linked list by rewiring its next pointers, and return the new head.

tests.explain: Every arrow is turned around, so 5 becomes the head and 1 the tail.
An empty list (head = null) stays empty: return null.

hints: Don't create new nodes: walk the list once and turn every next pointer around.
Keep two pointers, prev (the already reversed part, starting at null) and curr (the next node to flip).
Before you overwrite curr.next, save it. Then set curr.next = prev, move prev to curr and curr to the saved node. When curr is null, prev is the new head.

complexity.time: O(n): each node is visited once
complexity.space: O(1): three pointers (the recursive version uses O(n) call stack)
